title: The Mineral That Moves the Board — Eddie Would Go

u.El Mineral que Mueve el Tablero: The Mineral That Moves the Board
u.El uranio dejó de comportarse como una c: Uranium has stopped behaving like a commodity administered by engineers and long-term contracts. It is today a strategic asset in dispute: the states that have it want to control it before others do, the investors who could develop it demand a legal certainty that is in short supply, and reactor operators in Europe, Asia and North America cannot find enough ore to buy. This article is about how that assumption broke, who paid the cost, and why a mine on the Patagonian plateau now comes up in investor conversations in Toronto, Islamabad and Sydney.
u.«El equilibrio es la excepción, no la re: «Equilibrium is the exception, not the rule.»
u.— Ilya Prigogine, Nobel de Química 1977: — Ilya Prigogine, Nobel Prize in Chemistry 1977
u.En noviembre de 2025, un convoy con apro: In November 2025, a convoy carrying approximately 1,000 tonnes of uranium concentrate left Arlit, in northern Niger, crossed into Burkina Faso and made its way to the outskirts of the port of Lomé in Togo. A Russian freighter waited at anchor off the coast. The uranium never arrived. Togo blocked its passage. The ship waited weeks and left empty. The material was returned to a military base near Niamey. The French company that had mined that uranium for decades learned about it from the press.
u.Esa imagen —un carguero varado frente a: That image — a freighter stranded off an African port, waiting for a cargo the international order managed to stop but not recover — sums up precisely the state of the global uranium market in 2026. The assumption on which the market was built — that Kazakhstan would keep growing linearly to cover demand — is broken. Nobody declared it officially. It simply stopped being true.
u.I. El árbitro que no puede arbitrar: Kaz: I. The arbiter that cannot arbitrate: Kazakhstan
u.Kazajistán controla alrededor del 40% de: Kazakhstan controls around 40% of the global primary uranium market. That is not supply diversification. It is risk concentration. Over the last decade the market bet that Kazatomprom would keep growing linearly — accumulating share, opening deposits, expanding capacity — to satisfy a demand that, at the same time, nobody had foreseen would grow so fast. That bet is lost on three fronts simultaneously, and none has a quick fix.
u.El primero es físico. La minería kazaja: The first is physical. Kazakh mining is done almost exclusively by in-situ leaching: acid solutions are injected into the subsoil to dissolve the uranium and pump it to the surface. The process is intensive in sulphuric acid, and Kazakhstan does not produce enough. A new plant with a capacity of 800,000 tonnes a year has been under construction at Taikonur for years; financing was only secured in 2025 and the timetable continues to run with no firm delivery date.
u.El segundo es el proyecto estrella que n: The second is the flagship project that failed to deliver. Blocks 6 and 7 of the Budenovskoye deposit were the engine of the promised growth: ~5,900 metric tonnes in 2025, scaling to full capacity of 6,000 tonnes in 2026. The blocks remain far from those numbers. The deposits are almost twice as deep as Kazakhstan's other leaching projects — which complicates the process — and contain more carbonates than expected, driving acid consumption higher still. According to official guidance published in the 2025 annual report, Kazatomprom projects production of between 32,200 and 34,000 metric tonnes in 2026, against the ~38,600 that appeared in its subsoil agreements two years ago: a difference of between 4,500 and 6,350 metric tonnes the market has already written off as lost.
u.El tercero es geopolítico, y es el que m: The third is geopolitical, and it is the one that most discomfits Western buyers. In late 2022, Rosatom acquired 49% of Budenovskoye through its subsidiaries. Kazatomprom's CEO, CFO, COO and CCO resigned within 18 months, arguing that the lack of transparency violated their fiduciary obligations. In late 2024, Uranium One — another Rosatom subsidiary — also sold its stake in the Zarechnoye deposit to a company linked to the Chinese state nuclear corporation. All Budenovskoye production is contracted to Rosatom until 2026.
u.Lo que queda para el mercado occidental: What is left for the Western market is not the bulk of Kazakh production. It is what remains after China and Russia have their contracts secured.
u.Para colmo, Kazajistán decidió construir: To make matters worse, Kazakhstan decided to build its own nuclear plants, choosing Rosatom for the first and China for the second. The country that ought to be the arbiter of the global uranium market is, in practice, committed to the two actors the West is trying to exclude from the nuclear fuel cycle.
u.II. El modelo que colapsó: Níger: II. The model that collapsed: Niger
u.En julio de 2023, el general Abdourahama: In July 2023, General Abdourahamane Tiani overthrew President Mohamed Bazoum in Niger. In market terms, the consequences took time to be understood. Niger represents less than 5% of world primary production — not a number to frighten analysts. But in 2022 it supplied 25% of the uranium feeding Europe's nuclear plants, with a peculiarity that is hard to replace: France, which generates around 70% of its electricity from nuclear power, depended on Niger structurally. The company operating the mines was Orano, majority-owned by the French state and present in the country for half a century.
u.Lo que siguió al golpe fue un desmantela: What followed the coup was a methodical dismantling of the colonial concession model. The regime blocked exports, closed borders and rejected Orano's offer to evacuate the uranium by air. In June 2023 it revoked the development licence for Imouraren — one of the largest deposits in the world. In December 2024, Nigerien military forces took operational control of the Arlit site, leaving Orano without access to its own facilities despite officially retaining 63.4% of the capital. An ICSID tribunal ordered on 23 September 2025 that Niger neither sell nor transfer the accumulated uranium. The regime ignored the ruling.
u.El intento de mover el material, que es: The attempt to move the material, which is the scene that opens this article, ended with the Russian freighter MV Matros Shevchenko waiting weeks off Lomé and returning empty. Orano, which had worked those mines for decades, learned of the entire operation from the press. At the time of publication of this article, the material remains on Nigerien soil, blocked by the ICSID ruling that Niamey cannot altogether ignore without closing off access to any international financial system it might want to use.
u.El contrato que Orano firmó, operó duran: The contract Orano signed, operated for decades and lost in twelve months was not a design anomaly. It was the industry standard model. If it can collapse like that, the risk of investing in new production in politically complex jurisdictions reprices upwards — permanently.
u.Lo que hace al caso nigerino más perturb: What makes the Nigerien case more disturbing than an ordinary investment dispute is what it reveals about systemic risk. Rosatom has already signed a cooperation memorandum with Niger. Among the speculated buyers for SOMAÏR's uranium are Turkey, China and Iran. And the pattern repeats: Mali and Burkina Faso, also under military juntas that expelled French security forces, are reviewing mining agreements in gold, manganese and rare earths. The paradoxical result is that the crisis taking uranium out of the market in the short term also makes the solution to the deficit more expensive and slower in the long term.
u.III. La oportunidad sin permiso: Argenti: III. The opportunity without a permit: Argentina
u.Hay 4.420 toneladas de uranio con recurs: There are 4,420 tonnes of uranium in reasonably assured resources beneath Cerro Solo, some 200 kilometres from Gastre, on the central plateau of Chubut. The CNEA has known for three decades that they are there. Argentine uranium production ceased in 1995 with the closure of Sierra Pintada, in Mendoza, and since then the country has imported around 220 tonnes a year to operate Atucha I, Atucha II and Embalse. Argentina has the largest uranium deposit in its history 200 kilometres from a provincial road and imports the material from Kazakhstan and Canada. Until three years ago, that paradox mattered to nobody outside the CNEA. Now it matters to YPF, to Milei and to 50 international investors who heard the pitch in New York.
u.El argumento que YPF Nuclear lleva a los: The argument YPF Nuclear takes to the markets has three layers. The first is geology: Cerro Solo allows estimated production of between 500 and 550 tonnes a year, twice domestic demand, with real margin to export the surplus. The second is the model: selling modular reactors with a commitment to purchase Argentine uranium included — what Horacio Marín calls the «Gillette model», where the margin lies not in the machine but in the refills. The third, and the most differentiating, is technological capability: INVAP — the state company based in Bariloche — designed the ACR-300, a 300-megawatt modular reactor conceived to supply data centres and industrial projects. Argentina is one of the few countries in the world that designs and exports nuclear reactors.
u.Pero entre el argumento y la producción: But between the argument and production lie four unresolved problems. The first is governance: the CNEA holds the concessions over Cerro Solo and another 18 projects in Chubut. Governor Ignacio Torres formally summoned the CNEA in 2025 to transfer those concessions to the province. YPF Nuclear wants to operate. Three actors with different mandates, different calendars and no signed agreement.
u.El segundo es legal. La Ley XVII Nº68 pr: The second is legal. Law XVII No. 68 prohibits open-pit metalliferous mining in Chubut. The provincial government argues that uranium is not a metalliferous mineral. But the trap lies in the geology: the CNEA determined that Cerro Solo is unsuitable for in-situ leaching because of hydrogeological conditions. The optimal method according to its own technicians is an open pit of some 60 metres followed by underground extraction. That method collides with the spirit of the law. The provincial legislature — which in 2021 repealed a mining reform within 72 hours under pressure from the street — is the arbiter. That debate has not begun.
u.El tercero es el antecedente vivo. En 20: The third is the living precedent. In 2021, Mariano Arcioni's government legislated a mining zoning plan for Chubut. Protests in Esquel, Trelew, Comodoro Rivadavia and Puerto Madryn repealed it in less than a week. Torres has a better relationship with the electorate and the global context is incomparably more favourable to the nuclear argument. But the institutional memory of that episode exists.
u.El cuarto es el tiempo. YPF apunta a com: The fourth is time. YPF aims to begin operations in 2030. Standard timelines for a uranium mine run between five and eight years in conflict-free jurisdictions. In a jurisdiction with a disputed legal framework, without social licence built and with three actors lacking a governance agreement, the realistic range extends. The global uranium deficit is a problem the market needs to solve in the second half of this decade. Argentina could be part of the solution in the first half of the next.
u.Lo que le falta a Argentina no es geolog: What Argentina lacks is not geology or technological capability. It is the agreement between Gastre, Rawson and Buenos Aires over who commands the subsoil of the plateau.
u.IV. La aritmética que no cierra: IV. The arithmetic that does not add up
u.La demanda mundial de uranio ronda las 7: World uranium demand runs at around 79,400 to 81,600 metric tonnes a year. Global primary production in 2025 was around 73,500 metric tonnes — 90% of requirements. The gap is covered, for now, by inventory accumulated during the years that followed Fukushima. That inventory is at critically low levels. It is not that it has run out. It is that it no longer suffices to absorb another shock.
u.El Sprott Physical Uranium Trust acumula: The Sprott Physical Uranium Trust holds around 35,800 metric tonnes of physical uranium — almost two years of demand from all American reactors. That number looks reassuring until one examines who controls it. It is not operational inventory distributed among utilities and operators. It is material concentrated in the hands of a financial vehicle designed precisely to take it out of the market and appreciate it. The uranium problem in 2026 is not one of total quantity in existence. It is one of who controls what, in which jurisdiction, and on what conditions they are willing to sell it.
u.Goldman Sachs proyecta déficits estructu: Goldman Sachs projects cumulative structural deficits of almost 907,000 metric tonnes between 2025 and 2045. Long-term contracts in 2025 were already being negotiated at between 86 and 90 dollars a pound. The incentive price for new greenfield capacity is consistently estimated above 100 dollars. The gap remains open.
u.Lo que la inteligencia artificial agregó: What artificial intelligence added to that equation was not a vague future demand. It was a present, urgent demand with a cheque in hand. Every large data centre consumes between 20 and 100 megawatts of continuous power. Operators do not want intermittent energy. Nuclear is the only technically viable answer at that scale on those timelines. Every reactor announced to feed an AI campus is future demand the market has to cover. The market does not know how.
u.El uranio llegó a la mesa de negociacion: Uranium arrived at the negotiating table between powers as bargaining currency. Not as a commodity. As leverage.
u.Mientras tanto, en Islamabad, los mediad: Meanwhile, in Islamabad, the Pakistani mediators remain in the room. What the United States is negotiating with Iran — 20 billion dollars in exchange for 440 kilograms of uranium enriched to 60% — is not, strictly speaking, a market operation. But the image says something that supply and demand models cannot represent. Uranium arrived at the negotiating table between powers as bargaining currency between a state under sanctions and the only superpower that can lift them. Not as a commodity. As leverage.
u.Ese desplazamiento —del mercado a la geo: That displacement — from market to geopolitics, from contract to decree, from commodity to sovereignty asset — is the structural change underlying all the stories in this article. The convoy halted on the outskirts of Niamey, the freighter that left Lomé empty, the four executives who resigned in Kazakhstan, the mediator in Islamabad with fissile material as bargaining currency: these are different images of the same displacement.
u.Argentina está en ese mapa por una razón: Argentina is on that map for a reason it did not choose: it has the mineral, it has the technology and it has institutions which, for all their fractures, remain recognisable to an investor coming from negotiations with Niamey. That is no small thing. But the comparative advantage of having rules only holds if the rules work. The triangle between Gastre, Rawson and Buenos Aires is not a technical problem of coordination between agencies. It is the first test of whether Argentina can turn a geological paradox into a political decision. The subsoil of the plateau has been waiting three decades for that answer. The world has needed it for three years.
